status: Closed — canonical recursive scope fixture and residue regression verified
area: Runner publication / temporary-lock residue classification test
finding: runner-publication-residue-classification.test.ts modeled temporary framework lock scope with bare directory names such as packages/cli/dist. The canonical write-scope policy intentionally treats a bare directory as an exact path and requires dir/** for recursive child authority, so the fixture's live lock did not own packages/cli/dist/atm.js and falsely failed before residue classification assertions ran.
expectedBehavior: A fixture that models ownership of generated descendants must use the same explicit recursive dir/** scope used by governed task cards. The stale fixture remains explicitly stale, so the test continues to distinguish foreign-live, unowned, and stale-recovery publication outputs.
evidenceOrRepro: On 2026-09-02 the unmodified test failed with expected ATM-FRAMEWORK-TEMP-g9 but actual undefined at the live-lock assertion. readFrameworkTempLockProjection correctly returned the lock, but frameworkTempLockOwnsPath delegated to pathMatchesWriteScope, which only matches descendants for scopes ending in /**. Existing task scopes and runner publication amendments use packages/cli/dist/** and release/atm-onefile/**. The repair makes the fixture use those canonical recursive forms.
containment: This changes only fixture scope syntax. It does not broaden pathMatchesWriteScope, relax write-ticket authority, alter runner publication ownership, or change any production command.
followUp: Closed after the focused residue-classification regression passes with the live and stale dispositions still asserted. Keep fixture scopes canonical: bare paths are exact, while descendants require /**.
